children: Nasdaq said it would invest $100 million in Payward, the parent company of crypto exchange Kraken, to build out infrastructure that will help capital and assets move across the financial system efficiently with durable liquidity.

Under the expanded partnership, both companies will aim to advance their work on the Nasdaq Equity Token, or NET, framework and also enter into a new market surveillance agreement. Specifically, Nasdaq said the partnership would support the continued evolution of tokenized market infrastructure while maintaining an issuer-centric approach that the exchange said is grounded in strong governance, regulatory compliance, and market integrity.
The companies will look to advance the operational and commercial infrastructure supporting NETs with plans to launch in the second quarter of 2027.

Earlier this year, Nasdaq said it would work with Kraken and issuing companies in developing its plan to offer tokenized stocks on its exchange. Nasdaq said plans for tokenizing stocks and other exchange-traded products would focus on corporate governance and look for ways to simplify or automate proxy voting or corporate actions such as dividend payments. The framework is expected to launch early next year.
